questions.question: In Object-Oriented Programming (OOP), what is the relationship between a Class and an Object?
options: An object is the blueprint, while a class is a variable
A class is a reusable code template (blueprint), while an object is a real, live instance created from it
Classes are functions; objects are dictionaries
questions.explanation: Spot on! The Class is the virtual design pattern (like a blueprint for a house), and the Object is the actual item built from that design.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the special built-in constructor method '__init__' inside a Python class?
options: To initialize and set up starting attributes and values for a new object automatically upon creation
To print text statements to the screen
questions.explanation: Correct! The __init__ constructor runs automatically when a new object is instantiated, defining its baseline properties.

questions.question: Which Python library is extremely useful for sending automated HTTP requests (like GET and POST) to fetch content from web servers?
questions.explanation: Excellent! The 'requests' library allows your Python script to communicate with external web services and scrape websites.

questions.question: In our Ping Pong game built with the Turtle library, what is the default coordinate location of the turtle pen when the screen first launches?
options: At the center of the screen (0, 0)
questions.explanation: Great! Turtle graphics uses a standard cartesian graph where the center of the drawing window is located exactly at coordinates (0, 0).

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Write Python code to import the 'turtle' library, and initialize a game screen object named 'win' by calling the turtle.Screen() constructor.
questions.task_hint: Write: import turtle then win = turtle.Screen()
questions.explanation: Perfect! Importing turtle and setting up Screen() creates the visual canvas window needed to draw shapes or build games.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Define a basic Python class named 'Student' with an initializer constructor method '__init__' that takes the parameter 'name' and stores it as an instance attribute: self.name = name.
questions.task_hint: Write: class Student: def __init__(self, name): self.name = name
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Creating constructors and assigning parameter values to 'self' is the foundational way to initialize custom object attributes in Python.
